zenith

ZEE-nith · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Zenith is the highest point or state of something, especially of power, success, or achievement.

By the 1960s, the airline had reached the zenith of its popularity, with flights booked solid for months in advance.

Worked Example

Historians mark the mid-1400s as the zenith of the empire's power, when its territory and influence stretched across three continents.

Zenith describes the very peak moment of power or success -- often a point historians look back on as the best a person, company, or civilization ever achieved.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

high point: A high point is the everyday, all-purpose term for the best moment of anything — a trip, a season, a single afternoon. A zenith is grander: the towering peak of power, fame, or success, usually named by people looking back after the decline.

climax: A climax is the most intense moment a sequence of events builds toward — a story's final duel, a symphony's last chord. A zenith is not about tension but standing: the highest level of power or success something ever reaches.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

nadir: the lowest point in someone's fortunes

decline: a gradual fall in strength, quality, or importance

Where it sits · how high the achievement climbs — success → zenith → apotheosis

success vs. zenith: Success is much milder than a zenith: it means achieving a goal at all, while a zenith is the single highest point a career or a power ever reaches.

apotheosis vs. zenith: Apotheosis climbs past even a zenith: a zenith is the real peak of power or success, while an apotheosis treats the peak as almost god-like, beyond ordinary human achievement.

Build the Word

The pieces

origin — samt

origin — samt: path, direction overhead (Arabic samt ar-ra's, via medieval Latin cenit)

Put it together

Put it together: Zenith comes from Arabic samt ar-ra's ('the path over the head'), an old astronomy term for the point in the sky directly overhead -- the highest point possible -- which came to mean the peak of power or success.

Use the root in a new word: Zenith (the brand)

Use the root in a new word: Zenith (the brand): In the twentieth century, 'Zenith' was also a popular brand name for radios and televisions -- fitting, since the name was meant to suggest the very top of quality.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Zenith is most often used for a peak moment of power, popularity, or success -- especially one that historians or critics look back on after the fact, once the decline that followed makes the peak clear.
